ca_trashcan_rock_east_face.blurb: This short trad face is part of Trashcan Rock in the Quail Springs area of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,200 feet. The wall sits only a few feet from the parking lot and looks out onto the paved road. It has seven routes, nearly all cracks, running from an easy 5.5 up to a hard 5.11, with a cluster at 5.8 and a couple at 5.10. The rock as a whole sees a lot of top-roping, and every route finishes with a walk-off. The formation's other face holds many more, mostly easier, climbs.

ca_atlantis_wall_left.blurb: The left section of Atlantis Wall sits near the south end of the Lost Horse area in Joshua Tree National Park, at roughly 4,100 feet. It is a short, steep wall holding seven routes: five trad and two top-ropes, graded from 5.7 to 5.11. Most of the lines follow cracks, with the odd face climb mixed in. It is the first section you meet on the walk in. The wall lies in a narrow canyon blocked at one end, so air barely moves and warm days feel hot. Descent is a walk-off down the gully beyond the formation.

ca_b_52_rock.blurb: B-52 Rock is a small dome in the North Wonderland part of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,130 feet. Climbing here is mostly traditional: six trad routes and one top-rope, graded from 5.6 to 5.11, with a pair at 5.8 and a pair at 5.10. The dome has two climbing faces. To reach it, take the path toward Reggie Dome from Keys Corner and continue to the next dome along, which is a walk of roughly fifteen to twenty minutes.

ca_b_1_boulder.blurb: B-1 Boulder is the dominant block in the Sentinel Boulders, in Yosemite Valley at about 4,000 feet. It has seven problems, all on the hard side: two at V4, two at V6, two at V7 and one V8. A large cave dominates one side, and roof problems start from jugs and pockets beneath it before topping out above. A long traverse starts nearby. Problems run up to about seventeen feet tall, so pads are the only protection, and shorter climbers may find the top-outs reachy.

ca_awk_boulder_the.blurb: The Awk Boulder is a tall block with big blobs along its top, in the Incognito Boulders cluster of Snow Valley West, near Running Springs in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 6,100 feet. It is a short stroll from the parking area. Seven problems run from very easy up to V6, with a spread of V0 to V3 and one hard line. Rounded, sloping holds reward technique over strength. Landings are flat and good. Only some faces are clean; the dirtier sides see little traffic and are not currently climbable.

ca_atom_smasher_boulders.blurb: Atom Smasher Boulders are a group of very large, cleanly split blocks in the north Wonderland part of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,100 feet, close to the Ivory Towers and Timbuktu Towers. Climbing is mostly trad on bolt-assisted lines, with one sport route and one top-rope among seven routes in total. Grades run from 5.9 to 5.12, with a moderate at the low end and several 5.11 and 5.12 lines above it. Expect a long, flat, sandy walk in of about an hour.
ca_atom_smasher_boulders.approach: Follow the North Wonderland trail beyond the Middle Kingdom, where it bends east and gets sandy. Turn left then right at the wash junction, pass Hooter Rock on your right, and the boulders sit a little farther east, partly hidden. Plan on about an hour.

ca_b_boulder.blurb: The "B" Boulder is the last boulder on the left at the back of the Windy Boulders South outcrop in Culp Valley, San Diego County, at about 3,000 feet. It is a short walk from the road. Seven problems range from V0 up to V6, mostly in the V0 to V4 band with one standout hard line. The boulder is shaded in the afternoon and has a good landing with little cactus nearby. The rock is sharp, so bring tape.
